title: Insecure deserialization runner: detect vulnerable Java, PHP, Python, and .NET deserialization endpoints
goal: WebGoat has a dedicated deserialization module. Insecure deserialization is OWASP A08:2021 and has enabled some of the most severe RCE exploits (Java Apache Commons Collections, PHP object injection, Python pickle). Implement a deserialization-probe runner: (1) Java detection: identify Java serialized object markers (0xACED0005 in base64: rO0AB) in request parameters, cookies, or headers. Send known gadget-chain payloads from ysoserial (URLDNS probe only — DNS callback, NOT RCE). If DNS callback received → confirmed deserialization endpoint. Finding: 'Java Deserialization - Potential RCE (ysoserial URLDNS confirmed)'. (2) PHP object injection: inject PHP serialized strings (O:4:'Test':0:{}) into request parameters. Check for serialization errors in response indicating eval of attacker-controlled data. (3) Python pickle: check for endpoints accepting pickle data (Content-Type: application/x-python-pickle or cookie values starting with base64-encoded pickle magic bytes). (4) .NET ViewState: check for unencrypted/unsigned ViewState by decoding base64 ViewState and checking for absence of HMAC signature. (5) Node.js: check for node-serialize package usage patterns. All probes use detection-only payloads — URLDNS for Java (no command execution), error analysis for others. Active tier.
scope: WebGoat deserialization module + OWASP A08:2021. Current coverage: ❌ Not implemented. Java ysoserial URLDNS is the standard detection-only deserialization probe used by all major scanners.
